tools.name: navigate
tools.description: Navigate to a URL. Waits for the page to load, then returns where it ended up plus a page snapshot with interactive element refs. On a heavy page that snapshot is most of the cost of the call: if you only need to READ the page, pass snapshot:false and follow with extract_text or find, which is far cheaper. Use compact/depth to trim the snapshot the same way the snapshot tool does.

snapshot.description: Return a page snapshot (default true). Set false for just the URL and title.

compact.description: Compact snapshot: skip nav/footer/ads. Reduces size by ~70% on e-commerce sites.

depth.description: Max nesting depth to capture in the snapshot

tools.name: back
tools.description: Go back to the previous page in browser history.

tools.name: forward
tools.description: Go forward to the next page in browser history.

tools.name: reload
tools.description: Reload the current page.

tools.name: snapshot
tools.description: Capture a compact DOM tree of the current page. Interactive elements get numeric refs (use with click/type/fill_form/etc). Use target ref to scope to a subtree, depth to limit nesting. This is the tool for ACTING on a page — it is also the most expensive one here, because most of what it returns is structure. If you only need to read the page, use extract_text; if you know what you are looking for, use find. Reach for those first and snapshot when you need refs. Always returns the whole page, so call it when you no longer have the page view an action reply refers to.

target.description: Ref number to scope snapshot to a subtree

compact.description: Compact mode: skip nav/footer/ads, show only main content. Reduces snapshot size by ~70% on e-commerce sites.

tools.name: find
tools.description: Search the page for elements matching text, role, or CSS selector. Returns matching elements with ref numbers, surrounding context, and — for links — the absolute href, so you can navigate straight to a result instead of clicking through it. More token-efficient than a full snapshot when you know what you are looking for.

text.description: Text to search for (case-insensitive substring match)

role.description: Filter by element role (button, link, textbox, etc)

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: Take a screenshot of the current page. Use snapshot for interacting with elements — screenshots are for visual verification only.

tools.name: get_text
tools.description: Get the full, untruncated text content of an element by its ref number.

ref.description: Element ref number from snapshot or find

tools.name: extract_text
tools.description: Read the page as text, with tables rendered as markdown. Use this when you need to READ content — an article, a results table, a description — rather than act on it. Far cheaper than a snapshot, which spends most of its tokens describing structure you do not need for reading. Pass a ref to read just that section. Long text comes in parts: a reply that stops early says so, with the offset to continue from.

ref.description: Read only this element and its descendants

offset.description: Start at this character, to continue where an earlier reply stopped

tools.name: list_actions
tools.description: List just the interactive elements on the page — buttons, links, inputs — with their refs, without the surrounding tree. Use it to answer "what can I do here?" when you do not need full page structure. Much smaller than a snapshot.

tools.name: highlight
tools.description: Briefly outline an element in the page so the watching user can see what you are about to act on. Purely visual — it changes nothing.

tools.name: get_url
tools.description: Get the current page URL and title.

tools.name: click
tools.description: Click an element by ref number (from snapshot/find). Reports whether the page navigated, where it ended up, and the updated snapshot (on the same page, only what changed since the last whole page). If the click ran but the page could not be captured afterwards the call still succeeds and says so — it never reports a click that happened as a failure, so do not re-click on an error.

ref.description: Element ref number from snapshot or find

tools.name: type
tools.description: Type text into an input element by ref. Set clear to erase existing text first. Set submit to press Enter after typing. Reports whether submitting navigated the page.

tools.name: fill_form
tools.description: Fill multiple form fields at once. Each field identified by ref number and value. Major token saver vs individual type calls. Reports whether submitting navigated the page.

tools.name: select
tools.description: Select option(s) in a dropdown element by ref.

tools.name: hover
tools.description: Hover over an element to trigger tooltips or dropdown menus.

tools.name: scroll
tools.description: Scroll the page or a specific element. Returns where the page is now and an updated snapshot (only what changed since the last whole page, when that is smaller).

ref.description: Element ref to scroll (scrolls page if omitted)

tools.name: press_key
tools.description: Press a keyboard key, optionally with modifiers (Ctrl, Shift, Alt, Meta). Examples: "Enter", "Tab", "Escape", "a".

tools.name: drag
tools.description: Drag an element from one position to another.

toRef.description: Ref of target element to drop onto

tools.name: upload
tools.description: Upload a file to a file input element.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the file to upload

tools.name: click_by_text
tools.description: Click an element by its visible text content. No prior snapshot needed — finds and clicks in one call. Reports whether the page navigated, where it ended up, and the updated snapshot (on the same page, only what changed since the last whole page).

role.description: Filter by element role (button, link, etc)

index.description: Which match to click if multiple (0 = first, default)

tools.name: dismiss_modal
tools.description: Dismiss a modal, dialog, or popup overlay. Automatically finds common dismiss buttons (Close, No thanks, Skip, ×). Provide text to target a specific dismiss button.

text.description: Text of the dismiss button to click (e.g., "No thanks")

tools.name: list_tabs
tools.description: List all open browser tabs with their IDs, URLs, and titles.

tools.name: switch_tab
tools.description: Switch to a specific browser tab by its ID (from list_tabs).

tools.name: new_tab
tools.description: Open a new browser tab, optionally navigating to a URL.

url.description: URL to open in the new tab

tools.name: close_tab
tools.description: Close a browser tab. Closes the current tab if no ID is specified.

tabId.description: Tab ID to close (current tab if omitted)

tools.name: evaluate
tools.description: Execute JavaScript in the page context. If ref is provided, the element is available as "element" in the script. Returns the script result as JSON.

ref.description: Element ref — available as "element" in the script

tools.name: wait
tools.description: Wait for a condition: text to appear, text to disappear, or a CSS selector to match an element. Default timeout 10 seconds.

text.description: Wait for this text to appear on the page

textGone.description: Wait for this text to disappear from the page

selector.description: Wait for an element matching this CSS selector

tools.name: get_cookies
tools.description: List cookies for the current page or a domain. Values are withheld by default — you get names, domains and flags, which is enough to tell whether a session exists. Set includeValues only if the task genuinely cannot proceed without them: cookie values are live credentials, the user must approve releasing them, and they persist in this transcript afterwards.

includeValues.description: Request the actual values. Requires explicit user approval.

tools.name: set_cookie
tools.description: Set a browser cookie.

tools.name: console_logs
tools.description: Get browser console messages, optionally filtered by severity level.

tools.name: network_requests
tools.description: List recent network activity for the current tab: method, status, URL, type, size and timing, plus a requestId usable with network_request_body. Sensitive header values (authorization, cookies and the like) are redacted before they reach you.

urlFilter.description: Only requests whose URL contains this substring

method.description: Only requests with this HTTP method

status.description: Only responses with this HTTP status code

tools.name: network_request_body
tools.description: Fetch the response body of one request, by requestId from network_requests. Kept separate from the listing on purpose: bodies can contain credentials and personal data, so retrieving one is gated at a higher risk level than browsing the request list.

tools.name: dom_query
tools.description: Query the DOM using a CSS selector (read-only, CSP-safe, no eval). Actions: "list" returns matching elements (with the absolute href for links), "text" returns the full text of the nth match, "attr" returns one attribute across every match — use it to read hrefs from a result list and navigate to them directly, which avoids clicking through. To click a match, use the "click" tool with a ref from a snapshot, or "click_by_text".

action.description: What to do with matches (default: list)

attr.description: Attribute to read for "attr" (default: href). href and src come back absolute.

index.description: Which match to read for "text" (default: 0 = first)

tools.name: download_file
tools.description: Download a file from a URL or by clicking a download link element. Returns the filename and local path after download completes.

ref.description: Ref of a link element to download from

tools.name: list_downloads
tools.description: List recent browser downloads with their filenames, paths, and status.

limit.description: Max number of downloads to return (default 10)

tools.name: activity_log
tools.description: Get the recent command history — what actions the agent has taken, their success/failure, errors, and timing. Useful for self-diagnosis.

tools.name: ask_user
tools.description: Ask the user a question and wait for their answer. The question appears in the onbridge side panel next to the page you are working on, so the user can answer without leaving the browser. Use this when you need a decision you should not make alone — which of several results to pick, whether details you found are correct, how to handle something ambiguous. Blocks until the user answers or ~110s passes; on timeout it returns without an answer and you may retry or proceed. Do not use it for actions that need permission — those are gated automatically.

question.description: The question to show the user. Be specific and self-contained.

options.description: Optional choices to render as buttons. The user may still type a free-form reply.

tools.name: bridge_status
tools.description: Check whether the browser extension is connected and what it will currently allow. Use this first if a browser command fails unexpectedly, to tell a disconnected extension apart from a genuine page problem.
